instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a Brown-out reset (BOR) circuit. 
A BOR circuit is a type of digital circuit that monitors the supply voltage of a system and generates a reset signal when the voltage drops below a certain threshold. 
The purpose of the BOR circuit is to prevent the system from operating improperly when the supply voltage drops below a safe level.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: 
- a supply voltage signal (vcc)
- a reference voltage signal (vref)
- a reset signal (rst_n)

Outputs: 
- a reset signal (rst_n)

The module should also have the following parameters:

- vth: the threshold voltage for the BOR circuit

Your module should implement the following functionality:

- The circuit should monitor the supply voltage (vcc) and compare it to the reference voltage (vref).
- If the supply voltage drops below the threshold voltage (vth), the circuit should generate a reset signal (rst_n).
- The reset signal should be active low, meaning that it should be low when the system is being reset and high when the system is operating normally.
- The reset signal should remain low until the supply voltage rises above the threshold voltage (vth) again.

To implement the BOR circuit, you should use Verilog code to compare the supply voltage to the reference voltage and generate the reset signal when the supply voltage drops below the threshold voltage. 
You should then use a flip-flop to generate the output reset signal, which should remain low until the supply voltage rises above the threshold voltage again.
